pr_title: drivers: can: only copy frame data for non-RTR frames
pr_body:
Only copy frame data for non-RTR frames as RTR frames do not carry any data.

Fixes: #57002
pr_comments:

issue_context.title: can: incorrect RTR flag handling in incoming frames
issue_context.body:
Hello @henrikbrixandersen, @alexanderwachter, @martinjaeger 

I've just discovered that almost all CAN bus drivers assume that an incoming CAN frame with the RTR flag has a valid payload and copies data from FIFOs/registers up onto the stack.

Unfortunately this behavior is incorrect, since RTR mean that some data should be transferred FROM the node, not TO.

Thus, trying to copy CAN's frame data in the case of RTR is nothing but a waste of resources at best, or a security problem at worst ("disclose sensitive data"), since the payload from some old frame will be copied almost everywhere and/or machine check can be raised on some odd hardware.

Regards
Andrey VOLKOV
Linux Socketcan co-founder
comments:
Hi @henrikbrixandersen,

I also checked the sending routines a little harder, and the situation there is also "not so good": almost all drivers are trying to send data while  RTR is active.

Unfortunately this can cause an almost guaranteed panic, since the actual payload length is 0 (so possible "read out of the buffer boundary" case). Luckily for now, almost all current drivers pre-allocate packets with a maximum payload length, so you (I mean the team) have not seen this problem before and why it's probably not so critical. Meanwhile this is not the case when the device acts as a CAN router, then both incoming and outgoing traffic will contain RTR packets with zero payload in the Zephyr's CAN stack. Those, we will have a classic ping of death.

I've seen such situation before on Linux when someone from Freescale broke my MSCAN driver in their BSP by "optimizing" the RTR flag check.

Thank you for reporting these findings.

> I've just discovered that almost all CAN bus drivers assume that an incoming CAN frame with the RTR flag has a valid payload and copies data from FIFOs/registers up onto the stack.
> 
> Unfortunately this behavior is incorrect, since RTR mean that some data should be transferred FROM the node, not TO.

Right.

> Thus, trying to copy CAN's frame data in the case of RTR is nothing but a waste of resources at best, or a security problem at worst ("disclose sensitive data"), since the payload from some old frame will be copied almost everywhere and/or machine check can be raised on some odd hardware.

Zephyr is not a "multi-user" system, so the security problem is more theoretical than practical. However, we should not read potentially uninitialized data from the CAN controller MB/FIFO.

> I also checked the sending routines a little harder, and the situation there is also "not so good": almost all drivers are trying to send data while RTR is active.

Right.

> Unfortunately this can cause an almost guaranteed panic, since the actual payload length is 0 (so possible "read out of the buffer boundary" case). Luckily for now, almost all current drivers pre-allocate packets with a maximum payload length, so you (I mean the team) have not seen this problem before and why it's probably not so critical. Meanwhile this is not the case when the device acts as a CAN router, then both incoming and outgoing traffic will contain RTR packets with zero payload in the Zephyr's CAN stack. Those, we will have a classic ping of death.

In Zephyr `struct can_frame` is always allocated with full data size, so reading the data buffer, even for RTR frames, will not lead to a panic. However, it might result in writing uninitialized data to the CAN controller MB/FIFO, which should not happen.

I will look into providing a fix.

This issue has been marked as stale because it has been open (more than) 60 days with no activity. Remove the stale label or add a comment saying that you would like to have the label removed otherwise this issue will automatically be closed in 14 days. Note, that you can always re-open a closed issue at any time.

> FYI @grantramsay can_mcan.c is affected too.

Yes, I am working on a fix.

> > FYI @grantramsay can_mcan.c is affected too.
> 
> Yes, I am working on a fix.

It was mainly an alert for @grantramsay :). He had just worked on MCAN driver and probably still has access to the hardware. Therefore, he can probably fix and check RTR. Moreover, for MCAN driver, this error is not so low priority, but looks like a "ping of death": data fetching from Rx FIFO/pointers updating is based on the wrong DLC, so content of all following frames will be unpredictable.

> It was mainly an alert for @grantramsay :). He had just worked on MCAN driver and probably still has access to the hardware. Therefore, he can probably fix and check RTR.

No worries. I have access to a handful or more different boards from different vendors all implementing CAN controllers based on the Bosch M_CAN IP, allowing me to verify the changes across a wide range of different M_CAN IPs.

> Moreover, for MCAN driver, this error is not so low priority, but looks like a "ping of death": data fetching from Rx FIFO/pointers updating is based on the wrong DLC, so content of all following frames will be unpredictable.

That is not how the Rx FIFOs in the Bosch M_CAN work. FIFO elements are of a fixed size. Please avoid speculating the impact of issues like this as it just adds uncertainty and doubt.

This is purely an issue of reading and writing potentially unitialized memory regions.

review_comments:
I'm not sure if we need this one either.. Imo the user shouldn't try to read the data outside the DLC.

Is the concern that RTR frames have a non-zero DLC? Maybe we should drop these invalid packets in the driver?
The DLC of an RTR frame tells the recipient how much data to reply with. Please see the linked issue for the bug report.
But in this case, if the RTR flag is set the user should know that the data is invalid. I don't see why we need to zero out data bytes.
Otherwise we can leak uninitialized stack contents to the application/user mode thread.
The device will only the transmit the payload set by the DLC. I don't think we need zero to initialize the whole frame.
Zeroing the entire frame struct before filling in individual fields allows for future extensions to the struct without worrying about unitialized fields.
Could we then just zero out upto the data field? (the way I did on the receiver side)
No. The intent is to not leak uninitialized data from the ISR stack/kernel thread stack to the application/user mode thread - and vice versa.

For the transmit side, we should modify the spi transfer length so that it doesn't include the data buffer when RTR flag is set. This way we don't have to zero initialize the data. If you want, I can send in a separate patch for this so that you don't have to get everyone to approve again.

Btw I tested your patch on the mikroe mcp2518fd click and API test passes fine. (Although the receive rtr tests are skipped now because CAN_FILTER_RTR is not supported). I'll work on a patch to add this.

> For the transmit side, we should modify the spi transfer length so that it doesn't include the data buffer when RTR flag is set. This way we don't have to zero initialize the data. If you want, I can send in a separate patch for this so that you don't have to get everyone to approve again.

@talih0 Yes, that sounds like a nice improvement. Please submit this as a separate PR and let's try to get that into v3.5.0 as well.
